- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap peak values.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to adjust downward — apply downward bias correction in next 3–5 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model overestimates recovery — forecast should be capped at 1–2% below historical mean of recent 10-day range.
- When sentiment is bullish but supply net is negative, model often overreacts — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per event day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to drift upward — apply downward drift correction (e.g., -0.1% per day) until sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong rallies — add a 1–3 day decay factor to forecast slope (e.g., linear decay from peak to 10-day moving avg).
- When official events are frequent and supply net is negative, model overestimates price stability — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per event day until supply net stabilizes.
